At the left end, HuffPost amplified a pundit's charge that Republicans had "Disgraced Themselves," while the Los Angeles Times characterized Republican questioning as a "smear" attempt that Fauci "refuses to play." Both headlines position Fauci as a sympathetic figure resisting bad-faith attacks. Center outlets—AP, Bloomberg, and NeutralNews—used wire-style factual language, reporting simply that Fauci "invoked" or "pleads" the Fifth Amendment without characterizing motive. At the right end, The Free Press framed the Fifth Amendment as evasion rather than legal right, warning it "Won't Spare Fauci from the Truth," while Breitbart mocked celebrity support as "Cringe Overload" and USA Today's opinion page accused Fauci of putting "ego ahead of American lives." The key linguistic divide is whether invoking the Fifth Amendment signals a legal right or an admission of wrongdoing.
